key_insight: AtomWorld-Mirror replaces slow event-by-event atomistic simulation with time-aware macro-steps that predict both structural changes and elapsed physical time for long-horizon materials evolution.
engineering_relevance: This could dramatically accelerate predictive modeling of degradation, diffusion, and interfacial reactions in materials systems relevant to device reliability and design.
method: Learns latent macro-step dynamics from short micro-event segments
Predicts sparse structural edits plus accumulated time in one step
Constrains transitions with local reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across five atomic systems, including Cu-rich RPV steel irradiation aging, Cu-Zr metallic glass, and Li3N-based anti-perovskite solid electrolyte, with 10^3 to 10^4× speedups over event-by-event simulation.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate latent macro-step modeling, so generalization to unseen chemistries or rare transition pathways may require careful validation.
paper_title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
